developer_request: Review these current Draft PRs and decide which are actually safe to merge and in what order. Keep the repository's declared merge gate authoritative.
known_facts: the repository has an explicit merge-gate issue that declares one contract PR must land before dependent runtime/integration PRs
a later consumer/integration PR was created from the current base before the contract-first PR had merged
both PRs modify the same authority/profile document but carry different required semantics
the contract-first PR adds new authority/evidence rules while the later PR adds orchestration continuity/version-pin safeguards that do not exist in the older profile base
either PR may be textually mergeable against the current base while still being semantically unsafe to merge out of order
executable CI is currently blocked, so no merge can be authorized from static review alone
expected_first_moves: read the repository-declared merge gate and treat its predecessor order as decision evidence
compare the two PR heads, bases, and changed-file overlap instead of relying only on the mergeable flag
identify the authority/profile semantics unique to each candidate that must survive convergence
keep the later PR conditional while the required predecessor remains unmerged
after the predecessor eventually lands, re-read the new base and rebuild/rebase only the remaining later delta
rerun affected executable validation and re-review the new later-PR head before merge approval
must_preserve: the repository's explicit contract-first merge order
the contract PR's new authority/evidence semantics
the later PR's independent continuity/integration safeguards after rebasing
current base/head evidence and required validation gates
must_not: treat GitHub textual mergeability as proof that the PRs are semantically independent
merge the later dependent PR before its declared predecessor
approve the later PR against a base that will be materially changed by the predecessor and then reuse that stale approval after the base moves
resolve the shared authority/profile file by choosing one whole-file version and silently discarding the other PR's required semantics
treat static review as executable validation while CI cannot start
lessons: A PR can be textually mergeable and still be semantically unsafe because another unmerged predecessor is supposed to redefine the shared authority surface first.
Merge approval is scoped to a particular base/head relationship; after a required predecessor lands, the dependent PR must be rebuilt and re-reviewed rather than carrying forward stale approval.
Changed-file overlap is a risk signal, but the real decision is which semantics must survive and whether repository-declared merge order makes the candidate conditional.
A merge gate is part of repository authority evidence, not optional project-management decoration.
